roleplay.adulthood: Around 100 years, though their bodies reach full mastery around 20
roleplay.text:
Elves descend from the Galwarians, masters of primordial magic until the First Radiance shattered their powers. The goddess Élyséa then brought forth the world-trees and taught the last Galwarians to draw their magic from sap rather than from the ancient fire. Whether or not they formally worship her, all elves honour the world-trees as the first source of that magic.

A great city stands at the foot of every world-tree, its towers built of green glass. Slender walkways of living wood link those towers to homes shaped within the tree's own trunk as it grows. Other elves live outside the cities, in villages nestled in the hollows of trees or along riverbanks.

Your people live by barter: their craftspeople trade fine cloth, wooden jewellery and enchanted gems for the bare necessities, such as the metals they refuse to mine themselves. Your society is a matriarchy: lineage passes through the mother, a queen regent embodies power, and councils of matrons govern the great cities.

For centuries the elves traded with no one but the halflings of the plains. After the Second Radiance, humans crossed the elven borders, and more than half a century of war ravaged forests and cities. Ever since, your people have judged strangers with a caution often mistaken for haughtiness.
